rationale: Scrutiny standard, risk shared-core-two-harnesses. I reviewed the band change in draw.ts and its integration points in both harnesses: band() in Claude Code and render.ts bandNode in OpenCode. I also covered the pane, the run band and answer(), which the change must leave alone. Criteria a through g are each verified by the cited tests, the committed diff and three reused evidence records whose input fingerprints match the committed blobs at 2360caae. Neither judgement point violates a criterion. The completed-cycle rendering follows the pane's compact track, which criterion a names as governing and criterion e requires the band to reuse. Dropping the status glyph before the id at 20 columns follows an order that criterion d leaves open, and the current-phase cell still shows that glyph in the same key. No trust boundary is touched: the change is display-only and adds no capability, I/O or input path, so no specialist review applies. No blocking findings.
